## Fatty acid profile

The analysis of participant's blood profiles following n-3 fatty acid supplementation revealed a significant increase in various n-3 fatty acids. This observervation provides evidence of successful uptake and compliance.

Increased amount of Eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) (C20:5 n-3) (29,6 enheter, p<0,001), Docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) (C22:5 n-3) (4,5, p<0,001) and Docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) (C22:5 n-3 (18, p<0,001)): gjennomsnittlig endring i T2 korrigert for T1.

The analysis also showed a reduced amount of various n-6 fatty acids. What is worth to mention about this?

Reduced amount of Oleic acid (??) (C18:1 c-9) (-33,3, p=0,042), gamma-linolenic (C18:3 n-6), Dihomo-γ-linolenic acid (C20:3 n-6) (-5,8, p<0,001) and Arachidonic acid	(C20:4 n-6) (-17, p<0,001)

## Glucose metabolism assessment

To evaluate glucose metabolism, serum concentrations of glucose, c-peptide and adiponectin were measured. Assessments were conducted under fasting conditions as well as following (2 hours) the ingestion of a standardized amount of glucose (75 g of ??), ie. glucose tolerance test. Additional testing was perfomed one hour to detect any noteworthy peaks of interest. Notably, none of the test, including HOMA2, the glucose tolerance test, or c-peptide, revelead significant differences between the control and intervention groups.

Homeostatic model assessment (HOMA): What were the absoulute numbers in the different groups? This in regards to the cut off levels, ie how many had IR? What was their HbA1c-levels?

The diagnosis of diabetes in established when one or more of the following criterias are met: HbA1c >= 48 mmol/mol, fasting plasma glucose >= 7,0 mmol/L and/or glucose consentrations >= 11,1 two hours after a glucose tolerance test. If a patient presents with random plasma glucose >= 11,1 along with symptoms of diabetes, there is no neded for a repeat test before confirming the diagnosis. Our baseline data indicated that 10 out of 66 participants in the control group and 6 out of 61 participants in the omega-3 group had glucoe levels exceeding 11. Subsequent analaysis after 7 weeks of supplementation revealed about the same levels; 11 out of 65 and 7 out of 60, resp. Potential significance?

The mean serum glucose levels at baseline, before the supplementation period, were 4,4 mmol/L in the control group and 4,4 mmol/L in the intervention group. The average 2-hour values were 6,4 and 6,2, respectively. Following 7 weeks of supplementation, the baseline values were 4,7 mmol/L in the control group and 4,5 in the omega-3 group. The corresponding 2-hour values were 6,0 and 5,7, respectively. At the baseline time point, 2 out of 65 participants in the controll group had a higher glucose concentration higher than 11,0 mmol/L after 2 hours, ie. diabetes, while the omega-3 group has 1 out of 60. After 7 weeks, these numbers changed to 2 and 0, respectively.
